requirements.quote:
At a high level, an endpoint measures the time from when a packet was
   sent to when it is acknowledged as an RTT sample.
requirements.condition: When an endpoint obtains an RTT sample from an acknowledged packet
requirements.required_behavior: Measure the RTT sample as the elapsed time from sending that packet until receiving its acknowledgement.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not define that packet's RTT sample using different start or end events than packet transmission and acknowledgement.
requirements.error_behavior: No error behavior is specified in this excerpt.
requirements.why_checkable: A test can record the packet-send and acknowledgement-receipt timestamps and compare their difference with the implementation's RTT sample.

requirements.quote:
The endpoint uses
   RTT samples and peer-reported host delays (see Section 13.2 of
   [QUIC-TRANSPORT]) to generate a statistical description of the
   network path's RTT.
requirements.condition: When an endpoint generates its statistical description of a network path's RTT
requirements.required_behavior: Use both measured RTT samples and peer-reported host delays as inputs.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not construct the RTT description while disregarding either the RTT samples or the peer-reported host delays.
requirements.error_behavior: No error behavior is specified in this excerpt.
requirements.why_checkable: Implementation data flow or controlled samples with varying peer-reported delays can show whether both specified input classes feed the RTT estimation logic.

requirements.quote:
An endpoint computes the following three values
   for each path: the minimum value over a period of time (min_rtt)
requirements.condition: For each network path for which the endpoint computes RTT statistics
requirements.required_behavior: Compute a per-path min_rtt value representing the minimum RTT over a period of time.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not omit min_rtt or share a single min_rtt across distinct paths as though it were path-independent.
requirements.error_behavior: No error behavior is specified in this excerpt.
requirements.why_checkable: Tests can supply known RTT samples on separate paths and inspect whether each path has a minimum-valued min_rtt statistic.

requirements.condition: For each network path for which the endpoint computes RTT statistics
requirements.required_behavior: Compute a per-path smoothed_rtt as an exponentially weighted moving average.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not omit smoothed_rtt, compute it as a non-exponentially-weighted statistic, or share it across distinct paths as path-independent state.
requirements.error_behavior: No error behavior is specified in this excerpt.
requirements.why_checkable: A sequence of controlled RTT samples can distinguish exponentially weighted averaging from other calculations, and separate path inputs can verify per-path state.

requirements.quote:
the mean
   deviation (referred to as "variation" in the rest of this document)
   in the observed RTT samples (rttvar).
requirements.condition: For each network path for which the endpoint computes RTT statistics
requirements.required_behavior: Compute a per-path rttvar value as the mean deviation in the observed RTT samples.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not omit rttvar, calculate it as an unrelated dispersion statistic, or share it across distinct paths as path-independent state.
requirements.error_behavior: No error behavior is specified in this excerpt.
requirements.why_checkable: Known RTT sample sequences and separate path state allow comparison of the reported rttvar with the mean-deviation statistic described here.
